subject: Mounting an alternate file system with hdfs

messages.author: d7a934c791b29498
messages.subject: Mounting an alternate file system with hdfs
parts:
I have several Hadoop clusters.

I use RHadoop with one setup and in that system, rhdfs works as expected from the help files.

I can use commands such as

hdfs.ls(path="/", fs=hdfs.defaults("fs"))

and they work.

However, there is a second system run by a second administrator.  Normally I access it manually through the 50070 port of its hadoop namenode page.  The admin has set it up to follow the default hadoop documentation.

The NameNode front page is at http://namenode-name:50070/

From there I can manually browse the filesystem by manually following a hyperlink.

I would like to be able to enter an RHadoop command something like:


hdfs.ls(path="/", fs="http://namenode-name:50070/")

but that doesn't work.

I imagine that I might need to reset HADOOP_HOME and/or HADOOP_COMMAND, but trying to use http: in a configuration file doesn't seem to work.

Possibly I also need to alter my .xml files so that my RHadoop installation is looking for the remote namenode and datanodes on the second system.

Ideally, I would like to use one RHadoop system to look at multiple HDFS filesystems, but the highest priority is how to look at a remote HDFS filesystem.

Thanks.

messages.author: d7a934c791b29498
messages.subject: Re: Mounting an alternate file system with hdfs
parts:
Clarification:
Of course, when I manually browse the link, I get an hdfs connection to a different URL, and of course I have tried using the HDFS shell command as documented at:

https://hadoop.apache.org/docs/r0.18.3/hdfs_shell.html

but that does not appear to work.

When I use the HDFS commands as a normal shell, I get network timeouts.

messages.author: d7a934c791b29498
messages.subject: Re: Mounting an alternate file system with hdfs
parts:
Second clarification: Of course, I can over-write my old .xml files entirely and cause machine B1 to see cluster A.  That part is easy.  The problem is that there doesn't seem to be an easy way to set a parameter at runtime, without leaving R, in order to see clusters at A, or C, or D, or any other location accessible over the network.

If there were an easy way to do this at the R command line, that would have big consequences for various analysts at machines B1, B2 ... Bn.

Thanks.

messages.subject: Re: Mounting an alternate file system with hdfs
parts: Sorry I don't know how this fell through the cracks, actually I do know after studying group filters for an hour (or lack thereof). We don't have any other request for this feature. I thin the big advantage of hadoop is consolidation, and if you run n hadoops, so to speak, you may as well use mySQL. I am exaggerating, but you see my point. That said, if you wanted to develop this feature, I would be interested in reviewing your changes. I think both the multi-configuration and supporting the full URL syntax make sense, we would need to discuss pros and cons but configuration path is probably easier to implement. Before doing any coding, please enter an issue on the rmr2 issue tracker so that we can make some plans. Thanks
